messages:
sara: quick heads-up — got another support escalation this morning: customer saw repeated 429s and 'quota exhausted' spikes after a promo blast. they sent a repro but it's noisy; ran a focused internal load test to try and reproduce pattern. attaching notes + ask for alignment on sane defaults for RPM/TPM and burst handling.

michael: can you paste the repro steps/support payload? want to make sure we include the exact headers we check before we reply. support saw X-Request-ID + a bunch of 429s with different rate-limit headers.

sara: pasted below. customer did ~350 parallel short requests (chat completions) with average generated tokens ~60 per request over ~90s. headers they got: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 120`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 167` and intermittently `Retry-After: 12`.

alex: thanks — useful. i ran three internal runs: steady, bursty (500rps for 20s), and ramp (0->400rps in 60s). using `vegeta` with token-size emulation (60 tokens = ~300ms server work). command: ```vegeta attack -rate=400 -duration=60s -targets=targets.txt | vegeta report``` output (abridged):

-- steady 120rps (60s) --
Requests: 7200
Latencies (mean/p50/p95): 210ms / 180ms / 430ms
2xx: 7200
4xx: 0

-- burst 500rps for 20s --
Requests: 10000
2xx: 9800
4xx: 200 (mostly 429)
Latencies p95: 760ms
Observed token-use spike: ~30k tokens/min during burst window

jun: interesting — so under current per-key throttle (limit=120rpm, burst token bucket 3x) we see tail latency and then 429s when token bucket drains. shows we need either higher sustained RPM for typical app patterns or larger burst windows.

michael: for customer-facing playbook: what repro should support send? recommend a short `vegeta` snippet + header capture. e.g.:
```
GET /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <KEY>
Content-Type: application/json
{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":60}
```
Run 60 concurrent clients for 90s, collect `X-RateLimit-*`, `Retry-After`, and request ids. That should reproduce most quota exhaustion cases.

alex: propose defaults based on runs + typical customer patterns we saw across support:
- default per-key RPM: 180 requests/min
- default per-key TPM (token/min): 20000 tokens/min
- burst multiplier: allow 3x burst capacity for short windows (up to 30s)
- hard cap: 5x sustained limit but with exponential backoff enforcement
These are conservative but avoid false positives for marketing bursts.

jun: quick note on cost/abuse: 180 RPM + 20k TPM still allows heavier token spend if many large responses; we need split limits by endpoint (chat vs embeddings). embeddings use tokens differently; suggest embedding default TPM lower and RPM higher.

michael: for support triage we should add quick checks to identify whether 429 is from per-key throttle (X-RateLimit headers) vs global capacity fallback. suggested template:
- capture `X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset`
- if `Retry-After` present include it in ticket
- include `model` and `avg_output_tokens`
- run our `internal-repro.sh` (one-liner) and paste result

loadtest-bot: loadtest #1778932100 finished: 3 runs (steady, burst, ramp). artifacts: s3://redwood-loadtests/1778932100/ (logs + vegeta reports) :white_check_mark:

alex: other infra asks — we should add a small server-side metric that increases when bucket drains due to burst (label: `rate_limit.bucket_drain=true`) so support can differentiate bursts vs sustained overuse. also add trace sampling on 429s with request-body sketch (no PII).

sara: action items i can own: update support playbook with repro snippet + add a standardized reply template for burst 429s; create a short runbook for on-call with exact commands to run vegeta against a customer's key (sanitized) and how to interpret headers.

jun: i'll scope endpoint-specific defaults and propose embedding vs chat defaults by EOD. initial thought: embeddings RPM 400, TPM 8000; chat RPM 180, TPM 20000.

michael: can we surface a per-key recent-burst metric in console? even a simple 'recent burst count (30m)' would help CS when they ask.

alex: deploy-bot scheduled a canary with new throttle defaults to `staging` at 2026-03-15T16:10Z — canary will apply RPM/TPM: chat=180/20000 with 3x burst. will monitor `rate_limit.bucket_drain` and latency p95.

deploy-bot: canary started (id=cny-1778932100). rolling 10% of traffic to staging policy. expected observation window 30m.

sara: thanks. once canary metrics look stable we'll update docs and bump defaults for new API keys. for existing customers we'll recommend contact support for tailored adjustments. leaving notes here for posterity. :memo:
